t: 10 Reasons To Smile, Breathe Easy, And Not Let Stress Get The Best Of You et-stress-get-the-best-of-you/
q: Much of the stress teachers feel today comes from sources outside of the classroom.
Here at Smart Classroom Management we believe that the best approach to anything beyond your immediate control is laid-back acceptance.
Excitability among students is a major cause of misbehavior, but not among teachers who carry themselves with an all-is-well vibe.
Stress inhibits concentration, participation, and performance. A classroom free of tension, on the other hand, is the perfect incubator for learning
Being in the classroom is challenging enough without allowing events and decisions beyond your control to affect your peace and ability to manage and inspire your students.
Accept what you can’t change. Learn what you need to learn. And save your passion, your enthusiasm, and your energy for the classroom.

t: Why You Need A Good Relationship With Difficult Students cult-students/
q: Most teachers have a less-than positive relationship with difficult students—although it isn’t always evident to those around them.
The leverage you need to compel them to behave comes from your likability and general pleasantness. When they like you and trust you, they’ll want to please you.
Difficult students expect you to glare at them. They expect sarcasm. They expect you to be like all the rest.
They have an irresistible inclination to fulfill those labels, to become what is reinforced day after day.
Having a good relationship with difficult students is a choice you make that is 100% in your power to control. But it must come from you first.
You’ll have an opportunity to climb through the rubble, walk unchallenged past their defenses, and speak in both word and example directly into their heart.

t: How To Get Your Students To Do Their Homework https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2014/04/12/how-to-get-your-students-to-do-their-homework/
q: Homework can be particularly frustrating because it takes place outside of your presence.
It isn’t fair to them to struggle through work they don’t fully comprehend. Even one time will sap their motivation for completing future assignments.
As a result, their students become so accustomed to receiving immediate, extensive, and personal help that when it’s time to truly do it on their own, which is usually at home, they’re lost.
I recommend having your students set it out neatly on their desk as part of your morning routine.
This underscores the importance of building rapport and mutual likability with your students, while at the same time faithfully doing exactly what you say you will.

t: Why You Should Never Show Annoyance At Misbehavior misbehavior/
q: If you’re struggling with classroom management, then chances are you become annoyed when your students misbehave.
But every time you react emotionally to misbehavior, you shift control over to your students. You step out of the driver’s seat and hand them the keys.
The truth is, to have the well-behaved class you really want, you must maintain your deep care and concern for your students . . . while at the same time not give a whit if they misbehave.
It only works if it’s real. It only works if you truly feel it. If you have to force yourself to keep calm, the internal strife will inevitably bubble to the surface.
The secret is to rely exclusively on your classroom management plan. Let it do its intended job.
